article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Indica / 40% Sativa
Genetics: Pre-2000 Chronic × Warlock
Breeder: Gerrit of Magus Genetics
THC Content: 15–20%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , caryophyllene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Sweet fruit, wildflowers, honey, earth, spice
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late October
Indoor Yield: 350–650 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Double Dutch is a classic example of a marijuana strain whose growth pattern refuses to follow its genetic classification neatly. During vegetative growth, the plant looks unmistakably indica, building thick stems, broad leaves, and a compact bushy framework. Once flowering begins, however, that structure starts producing enormous elongated buds that resemble the oversized flower formations associated with sativa-dominant cannabis.

Created by Gerrit of Magus Genetics from a pre-2000 Chronic female and a Warlock male, Double Dutch became famous for those heavy flowers, its sweet wildflower aroma, and a high that combines cerebral elevation with substantial body relaxation. Serious Seeds eventually acquired the Magus Genetics collection and continues to preserve the cultivar today, describing it as a mostly indica F1 hybrid capable of approximately 350–650 g/m² indoors with an eight-to-nine-week flowering cycle. Its unusual mix of huge production, floral sweetness, and strong balanced effects also helped Double Dutch become an award-winning strain during the mid-2000s.
Genetics and Lineage

The authentic Double Dutch lineage is a pre-2000 Chronic female crossed with a Warlock male. Gerrit of Magus Genetics developed the hybrid during the early years of the twenty-first century, using Serious Seeds’ older Chronic genetics with his own established Warlock line. Serious Seeds now describes the cultivar as a stable, mostly indica F1 hybrid and explicitly preserves that original pedigree. The direction of the cross matters: Chronic is the female parent, while Warlock supplies the male side.

Chronic is central to the strain’s extraordinary flower production. Its contribution can be seen in the huge, elongated buds and sweet aromatic character that develop after the plant transitions into bloom. Warlock reinforces the indica structure, resin production, potency, and heavier physical side of the high. Serious Seeds notes that Double Dutch essentially grows like an indica while flowering in a way strongly reminiscent of Chronic. This division between vegetative and flowering behavior is one of the cultivar’s most distinctive genetic traits.

The family also ties together two important Dutch breeding programs. Magus Genetics supplied Warlock, while Serious Seeds supplied Chronic; after Magus Genetics became part of Serious Seeds, Double Dutch effectively returned to the company responsible for half of its original parentage. Serious Seeds now describes it as one of the major genetic treasures inherited from Gerrit’s breeding work.
Effects and Experience

Double Dutch produces a high that develops simultaneously through the head and body rather than moving strongly in only one direction. The initial mental effect can feel euphoric, bright, and pleasantly expansive. Conversation becomes easier, music may seem richer, and the mood often takes on a relaxed but socially comfortable character. There is enough cerebral activity to keep the strain from feeling dull, yet the experience generally avoids the racing stimulation associated with very Haze-heavy weed.

Physical relaxation arrives alongside that cerebral lift and gradually becomes more noticeable. The body can feel heavier without immediately becoming immobilized, making moderate doses suitable for an evening where relaxation is desirable but complete sedation is not. Historical Magus descriptions called the effect both cerebral and heavy, while Serious Seeds continues to describe the experience as complex and strong with both mental and bodily components.

Larger amounts shift the balance toward the indica side. Motivation can decrease, muscles feel heavier, and the experience may become more inward-looking. Historical material has placed THC around the mid-to-upper teens, while later cannabinoid records have shown examples around 19%. Because seed-grown cannabis can vary significantly, consumers should rely on the laboratory analysis of the specific flower rather than treating one THC percentage as universal.
Medical Benefits

The combined mental and physical character may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer a strain capable of promoting relaxation without producing immediate sleepiness. Some people may choose marijuana with this style of effect when dealing with temporary stress, physical tension, appetite loss, or discomfort later in the day. The cerebral portion may help maintain a more positive or engaged mood while the heavier side develops underneath.

Its balanced nature may also suit consumers who find very cerebral sativas overstimulating or heavy indicas too disabling. At moderate doses, Double Dutch can occupy the middle ground, bringing noticeable relaxation without completely eliminating mental activity. As dosage increases, however, the physical component can become considerably stronger.

Double Dutch itself has not been demonstrated in controlled clinical trials to treat any specific medical condition. Strain names also do not guarantee identical chemical profiles between growers. THC-rich cannabis may cause dizziness, anxiety, dry mouth, impaired coordination, or excessive sedation in some individuals, so medical consumers should use batch-specific cannabinoid testing and appropriate medical guidance when using weed to manage persistent symptoms.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Double Dutch has an unusually soft aromatic character compared with many strongly indica-dominant hybrids. Serious Seeds describes the aroma as fruity wildflowers, while the company’s historical discussion of the cultivar compares its sweetness to honeyed wildflowers inherited largely from Chronic. A properly cured flower can therefore smell like sweet fruit and flowering herbs rather than the aggressive fuel, hash, or skunk aromas associated with many heavyweight indicas.

Breaking the bud apart usually reveals greater depth. Earth, mild spice, herbs, and resin sit beneath the sweeter floral surface, while some phenotypes lean toward ripe fruit or a slightly acrid edge inherited from Warlock. The smoke is generally rich without becoming overwhelmingly harsh, and the sweetness can remain noticeable through the finish.

No single terpene profile represents every Double Dutch plant. Myrcene would be compatible with earthy fruit qualities, caryophyllene with subtle spice, and limonene with brighter fruit notes, while floral terpenes may help explain the characteristic wildflower aroma. These associations should be treated as sensory guidance rather than a fixed chemical formula; laboratory testing is required to identify the dominant terpenes of any specific batch.
Growing Information

Double Dutch is famous for changing dramatically once flowering begins. Vegetative plants develop wide leaves, thick stems, and bushy indica-style growth. During bloom, nearly every well-lit tip can swell into an enormous elongated flower cluster resembling a chain of dense popcorn-shaped buds. Serious Seeds warns that the side branches frequently require staking because the finished flowers can become exceptionally heavy. Supporting the plant early with stakes or a net is much easier than trying to rescue branches after they begin bending under mature buds.

The cultivar performs well in organic soil , coco , and hydroponic systems , giving growers considerable flexibility. Serious Seeds recommends roughly three-and-a-half to five weeks of vegetative growth before flowering and gives an indoor bloom period of eight to nine weeks. Potential indoor production ranges from approximately 350 to 650 grams per square meter, with high-performing examples capable of developing exceptionally large top buds. The breeder’s history even recalls Gerrit reporting individual plants producing around 140 grams under his indoor conditions.

Canopy management matters more than aggressive plant manipulation. Every branch that receives strong light has the potential to form a large cola, so topping, low-stress training, or a screen can increase the number of productive tops. Good airflow is essential once the flowers become dense, particularly late in the cycle. Outdoors, Serious Seeds places harvest around late October. Gardens in wet autumn climates should watch the interior of the oversized flowers carefully because their density can trap moisture.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Double Dutch?

Double Dutch is a cross of a pre-2000 Chronic female and a Warlock male. Gerrit of Magus Genetics created the original strain, and Serious Seeds now preserves and sells the genetics after acquiring the Magus collection.
Is Double Dutch indica or sativa?

It is a mostly indica hybrid, generally described as approximately 60–70% indica. Vegetative plants show broad leaves and bushy indica structure, while the flowering stage produces much larger, more elongated sativa-like buds.
What does Double Dutch taste like?
Sweet fruit and wildflowers dominate, often accompanied by honey-like sweetness, earth, herbs, and light spice. Serious Seeds specifically emphasizes its fruity wildflower aroma.
How long does Double Dutch take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately eight to nine weeks, or about 55–65 days. Outdoor crops generally mature around late October in the Northern Hemisphere.
Has Double Dutch won cannabis awards?

Yes. Double Dutch placed third in the Outdoor Cup at the 2006 HighLife Hemp Fair, second in the 2007 HighLife Hydro Cup, first in the Indica Grower category at the 2007 IC-Mag 420 Growers Cup, and second in the Indica Breeder category at the same year’s IC-Mag competition.
Final Thoughts on Double Dutch

Double Dutch earned its reputation by combining traits that do not normally appear together so neatly. Warlock gives the plant a thick-stemmed, bushy indica foundation, while Chronic transforms that structure during bloom by producing enormous sativa-style flower clusters. The contrast creates weed that is visually distinctive in the garden and highly productive without requiring an exceptionally long flowering cycle.

Its aroma also stands apart from the heavy hash, gas, and earth profiles often associated with indica-dominant cannabis. Sweet fruit and honeyed wildflowers form the center of the bouquet, followed by herbs, earth, and mild spice. Effects mirror the genetic balance, delivering noticeable cerebral uplift alongside a heavier body sensation rather than forcing the experience entirely toward stimulation or sedation.

For growers, the biggest consideration is simply supporting the crop. Nearly every well-lit branch can become heavily loaded, making stakes or netting important as flowering progresses. With eight to nine weeks of bloom, potential indoor yields reaching roughly 650 g/m², documented competition success, and genetics connecting Magus Genetics’ Warlock with Serious Seeds’ original Chronic, Double Dutch remains one of the more memorable high-yielding hybrids from classic Dutch cannabis breeding.
